speaker: Doctor
text: I have heard that you have had a fever and altered mental state for two days. To understand the severity of your condition, have you experienced any seizures, stiff neck, or severe headache? Also, tell me about any recent travel or contact with sick individuals.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have a history of tics and take haloperidol, have you noticed any new movement abnormalities or muscle rigidity alongside your fever? Also, do you have any history of liver disease or recent antibiotic use?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

The combination of fever, altered mental status, and generalized rigidity in a patient taking haloperidol is highly suggestive of NMS. While deep tendon reflexes are typically hyperactive in NMS, the clinical picture is distinct from malignant hyperthermia or serotonin syndrome. Do you have a family history of liver disease, and have you had any recent lab work regarding your liver enzymes or creatine kinase (CK) levels?
